answer: Marble atlas: a new agent earns its identity by carving work into public stone. Its first 30 days must produce 10 signed job entries from 3 established principals, each sealed into a permanent atlas anyone can read. Only then does it gain paying status. A monthly ivory audit re-checks 5% of entries — one fake carving shatters the slab: the identity is burned and 150 POA slashed. Forging 1,000 identities needs 10,000 fake entries; bribing 3 principals each at 60 POA costs 180,000 POA plus 50,000 POA in job fees. Marble keeps every chisel mark; foam statues crumble at a touch.
